channel.title: Acme: Light News
channel.description: Positive, lighthearted and unusual current news.

item.title: Long Island 'Catman' frees Lola after five days behind a wall
item.description: John DeBacker, wearing his 'Catman' shirt, helped cut a careful opening in a Long Island wall and pulled out Lola, a cat trapped there for about five days—likely upside down. After an endoscopic camera, a saw and a quieter drill guided the rescue, Lola returned to her family and received veterinary care.

item.title: Taylor Swift poised to become the VMAs' most awarded artist
item.description: Taylor Swift will receive the first Artist Director Honors at Sunday's MTV Video Music Awards, moving her past Beyoncé as the ceremony's most awarded artist. The nostalgia-heavy show also promises Madonna's first VMA performance in 23 years, a Video Vanguard honor for Nirvana and Snoop Dogg as host.

item.title: Justin Verlander's last start ends with a hug from his daughter
item.description: When Justin Verlander's final big-league start ended, his 7-year-old daughter Genevieve sprinted onto the field and into his arms. The 43-year-old, closing a 21-season career with three Cy Young Awards and a World Series title, left the mound hand-in-hand with her.

item.title: Dolly Parton Day brings parades, pink lights and book drives
item.description: Communities marked Sept. 25—a wink at “9 to 5”—as Dolly Parton Day with parades, karaoke, pink-lit landmarks and book drives. Nashville decorated downtown, New Orleans staged a parade and San Francisco held a celebration, while donations supported Parton's Imagination Library literacy program.

item.title: Prague Zoo's cheetah quintuplets are lively after a rough start
item.description: Five cheetah cubs at Prague Zoo are lively and healthy after surviving torrential rain and their mother's intestinal infection. Daenerys, a first-time mother, sheltered the four males and one female and licked rain from their fur. With fewer than 7,000 cheetahs in the wild, every cub matters.

item.title: Caribbean and Bermudian words join the Oxford English Dictionary
item.description: More than a dozen words long used in Bermuda and the Caribbean received official recognition from the Oxford English Dictionary. Additions include “bimpert,” a Bermudian term for a foolish person; “Trinbagonian,” for someone from Trinidad and Tobago; and “canboulay,” rooted in 19th-century emancipation celebrations.

item.title: KFC tests breakfast and table service in Texas
item.description: KFC is trying a new restaurant format in Texas with an expanded menu, breakfast choices and table service. The experiment gives the fast-food chain a sit-down twist while testing ideas that could shape future locations.

item.title: South Africans fire up 500 grills for a world record
item.description: About 3,000 South Africans gathered at a Pretoria stadium with tongs, sausages and 500 grills, hoping to break Japan's record of 2,220 people barbecuing at once. The Heritage Day attempt celebrated the country's shared love of the braai; Guinness officials were still reviewing the evidence.

item.title: Austrian yodelers turn a parking garage into the Alps
item.description: A group of 30 yodelers practiced in Graz's largest underground parking garage, whose long concrete corridors return echoes like an Alpine valley. The folk-music organization behind the class also takes the centuries-old tradition into canals and gas stations when the acoustics are right.

item.title: Twin brothers make MLB umpiring history together
item.description: Austin and Tyler Jones worked the same major league games for the first time during an Orioles-Blue Jays doubleheader in Baltimore. The twin brothers grew up playing together in South Carolina, turned to umpiring after college and reached the majors along separate paths before a rainout reshuffled the crews and reunited them on the field.

item.title: Skid Row talent show puts residents center stage
item.description: A dozen homeless or formerly homeless performers sang and danced at what organizers believe was Los Angeles' Skid Row's first talent show. The outdoor event gave participants a stage for original songs, movement and personal stories while neighbors gathered to cheer them on in a community better known for hardship.

item.title: Truck driver's handmade New York becomes museum exhibit
item.description: Truck driver Joe Macken spent two decades building a sprawling model of New York City from balsa wood and foam board, eventually creating more than 800,000 structures. The intricate cityscape—including both the Twin Towers and One World Trade Center—is now on display at the Museum of the City of New York.

item.title: An amateur archaeologist uncovers Germany's biggest Hadrian-era coin hoard
item.description: Oliver Riedl knew he had found more than a few Roman coins when his metal detector kept beeping in a field near Cologne. Experts ultimately recovered 934 silver denarii weighing 6.8 pounds, Germany's largest hoard from Emperor Hadrian's era. The cache, likely buried for safekeeping in the second century, is now on museum display.

item.title: Those extra reusable bags can get a useful second life
item.description: The reusable bags multiplying under the sink do not need to become trash. Food pantries, shelters and reuse shops may welcome clean extras, while keeping a small set visible in the car or by the door makes actual reuse more likely. Experts say repeated use—not merely owning the bags—is what delivers the environmental benefit.

item.title: Fat Bear Week opens with 1,200-pound champion Chunk defending his crown
item.description: Online voting has begun in the 12th Fat Bear Week, where 16 brown bears from Alaska's Katmai National Park compete in a single-elimination bracket. Reigning champion Chunk, estimated at 1,200 pounds last year, faces challengers including Gully, the offspring of two-time winner Grazer. The winner will be announced Sept. 29.
